usb_vendor_ids_source: Linux kernel USB audio quirk tables, sound/usb/quirks.c (d2636407bf8c, 2026-11-12) and sound/usb/quirks-table.h (e7c66b3e249e, 2026-11-04)
_the_robots_signal_and_the_decision_on_i: www.cambridgeaudio.com/robots.txt carries « Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference », then « User-agent: ClaudeBot / Disallow: / » across the whole site, and SEPARATELY « User-agent: Claude-User » with « Allow: / ». It distinguishes a training crawler from an agent reading on a person's behalf, and permits the second. Measured 2026-11-25 during a sweep of all 57 hosts this base cites - the only real conflict among them. Remi decided on 2026-11-25 that a Content-Signal of « ai-train=no, use=reference » is this project's permission to READ a page: « C'est reference. » Recorded in DECISIONS.md with its limits. What it permits: quoting a specification sentence in a sourced claim, with its URL and date - the use the signal names. What it does not touch: a prose clause forbidding reproduction. The 22 brands in the register of refusals stay refused, because a permissive robots.txt does not lift a sentence a lawyer wrote. So the five records under this brand stand on an affirmative basis: the host's own file allows the agent that read them, and its signal names reference as a permitted use twice over. They were never withdrawn, and this note replaces the provisional state they sat in for one afternoon.
_a_duplicate_brand_file_was_created_and_: On 2026-11-25 a second file, cambridge-audio.json with id cambridge_audio, was created here by mistake while writing the note above - a script that fell back to inventing a brand file when it could not find one at the filename it guessed. The five Cambridge records all carry brand « cambridge », which is THIS file. The duplicate was removed the same minute. It is recorded because the verifier did not catch it: its mutant suite tests that a record cites a brand that EXISTS, not that a brand file is cited by anything, so an orphan brand file passes every check and the brand count went from 327 to 328 with nothing but a stale documented figure to notice. A guard for brand files nobody cites would have caught it in one line.
